items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: So from then on I was playing all the jobs with him... We went back to his hard out at Manus Tavern... We played out there

ctx.x: But I know for one while there we had George Lewis and Slowdrag with us.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: how I come to get into the George Lewis band... So I went on a dead job with him that night... So he said, alright. He said, you stick with me.

ctx.x: Were you born right in the city?

Yeah, born in red right here in New Orleans. Only time I've been out of town is when the George Lewis band had trips away. And we've been very successful so far, so good, and I hope we continue to be that way until some of us start pegging out. And I started playing drums back in 1923.
Had you played any other instruments first? Any like guitar? No, no other instruments.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: He said, Joe, he said, how about joining up with me? ... I said, yeah, I said, I'll play with you ... I continued to play with him

ctx.x: Okay, well we're interviewing Joe Watkins this March 24th, 1969. Just going from what you're about to say, Joe, about when you started music.

When I started, I started in 1920s. Well that was quite a few years after George Lewis and Paul Barbrain. Well I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there. And I don't know about Joe Oliver because I always heard that Joe was not exactly from the Orlins. But it was him, Lee Armstrong, Funk Johnson, and you had Manuel Moneta. And, uh, was this other fella's name, uh, was a good…
What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: INTERVIEWEE: Yeah, that was, uh... Willow the Weeper and Mama Don't Laugh.

ctx.x: And I guess, uh, your first record was with Cuckoo. Yeah, that's right. Do you remember what was the first record tonight? First trumpet player was jazz, uh, Good Time Jazz. Good Time Jazz.
Yeah, that was, uh... Willow the Weeper and Mama Don't Laugh. Willow the Weeper, Mama Don't Laugh. Is he a red wing? No, Mama Don't Laugh.
